content.text: The eval stack's promise is one command with no credential in the file — those now conflict. Requiring the token with a loud message is the only option that keeps CLAUDE.md §11 intact:

python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path("docker-compose.ghcr.yml")
s = p.read_text()

s = s.replace('''#   docker compose -f docker-compose.ghcr.yml up
#''',
'''#   export OPENBAO_TOKEN=$(openssl rand -hex 16)   # see "Secret store" below
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.ghcr.yml up
#''')

s = s.replace('''# NOT for production: auth is disabled (AUTH_DEV_BYPASS), Postgres runs trust-auth
# (no password — so no credential ships in this tracked file) and Redis has none.''',
'''# Secret store: connection credentials go to OpenBao (ADR 0039), which replaced the
# plaintext RedisSecretStore — an evaluator following this file used to put real
# warehouse credentials into an unencrypted key-value store. A vault has no
# "no auth" mode, so unlike Postgres/Redis below it needs ONE value from you, and
# generating it here rather than defaulting it keeps every credential out of this
# tracked file (CLAUDE.md §11). The vault runs in dev mode: in-memory, so a restart
# drops stored credentials and connections must be re-entered.
#
# NOT for production: auth is disabled (AUTH_DEV_BYPASS), Postgres runs trust-auth
# (no password — so no credential ships in this tracked file) and Redis has none.''')

s = s.replace('''# names are non-secret identifiers. SECRET_STORE=redis (NOT env): api and worker
# are separate containers, and EnvSecretStore is per-process — a credential the
# api writes at runtime would be invisible to the worker (#86). Redis shares it.
x-app-env: &app-env
  DATABASE_URL: "postgresql+psycopg2://dataq@postgres:5432/dataq"
  REDIS_URL: "redis://redis:6379/0"
  SECRET_STORE: "redis"
  AUTH_DEV_BYPASS: "true"''',
'''# names are non-secret identifiers. SECRET_STORE=openbao (NOT env): api and worker
# are separate containers, and EnvSecretStore is per-process — a credential the
# api writes at runtime would be invisible to the worker (#86). The vault shares it.
x-app-env: &app-env
  DATABASE_URL: "postgresql+psycopg2://dataq@postgres:5432/dataq"
  REDIS_URL: "redis://redis:6379/0"
  SECRET_STORE: "openbao"
  OPENBAO_ADDR: "http://openbao:8200"
  OPENBAO_TOKEN: ${OPENBAO_TOKEN:?set it first — export OPENBAO_TOKEN=$(openssl rand -hex 16)}
  AUTH_DEV_BYPASS: "true"''')

openbao = '''  # Credential store (ADR 0039). Dev mode: auto-unsealed, in-memory, KV v2 at
  # secret/. OpenBao rather than HashiCorp Vault because Vault Community is BUSL-1.1,
  # which CONTRIBUTING rule 40 / ADR 0031 forbid us to distribute; OpenBao is the
  # Linux Foundation fork at the pre-BUSL point (MPL-2.0). The app speaks the KV v2
  # API, so OPENBAO_ADDR can point at a real Vault or HCP instead.
  openbao:
    image: openbao/openbao:2.6.1
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      # No default: a credential must never ship in a tracked file (CLAUDE.md §11).
      BAO_DEV_ROOT_TOKEN_ID: ${OPENBAO_TOKEN:?set it first — export OPENBAO_TOKEN=$(openssl rand -hex 16)}
      BAO_DEV_LISTEN_ADDRESS: "0.0.0.0:8200"
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8200:8200"
    cap_add:
      - IPC_LOCK           # lock memory so secrets cannot be swapped to disk
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "bao", "status", "-address=http://127.0.0.1:8200"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10

'''
anchor = '''  # One-shot: migrate to head THEN seed the dev user + probe fixtures + demo data'''
assert anchor in s
s = s.replace(anchor, openbao + anchor, 1)

s = s.replace('''  # Gets the full app env because the seed writes connection secrets via the
  # (redis-backed) SecretStore.''',
'''  # Gets the full app env because the seed writes connection secrets via the
  # (OpenBao-backed) SecretStore — hence the vault gate in depends_on.''')

p.write_text(s)
print("patched")
PYEOF
grep -n "openbao\|OPENBAO\|depends_on" docker-compose.ghcr.yml | head -25

# Create both from their templates on first run, then export so child processes
# inherit them regardless of working dir (alembic runs from backend/, so a
# CWD-relative dotenv lookup wouldn't find the root file).
step "Preparing .env / .env.app"
# Local-dev DB credentials are GENERATED here, never shipped in the tracked
# templates (those ship blank — we don't commit credentials, even mock ones).
# The password must match across both files: .env's POSTGRES_PASSWORD (the
# postgres container + the compose-built container DATABASE_URL) and .env.app's
# host-side DATABASE_URL (alembic/seed/uvicorn). user/db are non-secret
# identifiers; only the password is generated.
local_pg_user="dataq"
local_pg_db="dataq"
# Reuse a password already set in .env (so re-runs stay consistent); otherwise
# generate a fresh hex one (URL-safe — no special chars to encode in
# DATABASE_URL). `=..*` matches only a NON-blank value, so a blank line doesn't
# count as "set".
local_pg_password="REDACTED"
if [ -z "${local_pg_password}" ]; then
  local_pg_password="REDACTED"
fi

# Create each file from its template if missing, then BACK-FILL the local-dev
# creds whenever the key is still blank — covers a fresh copy AND a pre-existing
# file left blank (e.g. a manual `cp` of the now-blank template). Without the
# back-fill, a blank POSTGRES_PASSWORD trips compose's `${VAR:?}` guard / mismatches
# the host DATABASE_URL.
[ -f .env ] || { cp .env.example .env; ok ".env created from .env.example"; }
if ! grep -qE '^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REDACTED .env; then
  sed -i.bak \
    -e "s|^POSTGRES_USER=.*|POSTGRES_USER=${local_pg_user}|" \
    -e "s|^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REDACTED \
    -e "s|^POSTGRES_DB=.*|POSTGRES_DB=${local_pg_db}|" .env && rm -f .env.bak
  ok ".env local Postgres creds generated"
fi

[ -f .env.app ] || { cp .env.app.example .env.app; ok ".env.app created from .env.app.example"; }
if ! grep -qE '^DATABASE_URL=..*$' .env.app; then
  db_url="REDACTED"
  sed -i.bak -e "s|^DATABASE_URL=.*|DATABASE_URL=${db_url}|" .env.app && rm -f .env.app.bak
  ok ".env.app host DATABASE_URL set"
fi
set -a
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. ./.env
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. ./.env.app
set +a

# ── Conda environment ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Creating / updating conda environment 'dataq'"
if conda env list | grep -q "^dataq "; then
  conda env update -n dataq -f environment.yml --prune
  ok "Conda env updated"

# api/worker containers override DATABASE_URL + REDIS_URL to the in-network
# service hostnames in docker-compose.yml.

# Vendor-neutral backend (#589) — spans AND logs over OTLP/HTTP. This is the
# non-Azure path (#591): `docker-compose --profile telemetry up` starts a local
# Jaeger, then set this to http://jaeger:4318 (compose) or http://localhost:4318

AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID=
AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID=

# Only `marquez` is implemented (DataHub/OpenMetadata/Purview deferred behind the seam).
#   LINEAGE_PROVIDER=marquez

MARQUEZ_URL=

PROBE_SNOWFLAKE_ROLE=
PROBE_SNOWFLAKE_TABLE=
PROBE_SNOWFLAKE_SECRET_REF=

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# One-command dev environment setup from a fresh clone.
# Usage: ./scripts/setup.sh
# Requires: conda (miniconda/miniforge), docker, pnpm, git

set -euo pipefail

CYAN='\033[0;36m'; GREEN='\033[0;32m'; RED='\033[0;31m'; NC='\033[0m'
step() { echo -e "${CYAN}▶ $1${NC}"; }
ok()   { echo -e "${GREEN}✓ $1${NC}"; }
die()  { echo -e "${RED}✗ $1${NC}" >&2; exit 1; }

# ── Prerequisites ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Checking prerequisites"
command -v conda  >/dev/null || die "conda not found — install miniconda or miniforge first"
command -v docker >/dev/null || die "docker not found"
command -v pnpm   >/dev/null || die "pnpm not found — run: npm install -g pnpm"
command -v git    >/dev/null || die "git not found"
ok "Prerequisites OK"

# ── Local env files ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Two files (split in #209 so Settings can run extra="forbid"):
#   .env     — infra/compose only (POSTGRES_*, VITE_*); compose substitutes ${...}
#              from it and the postgres service reads it.
#   .env.app — app config (DATABASE_URL, AZURE_*, …); the file Settings reads.
# App code carries no DB credentials (config.py default is credential-less), so
# host-side tooling (alembic, seed, uvicorn) needs DATABASE_URL from .env.app.
# Create both from their templates on first run, then export so child processes
# inherit them regardless of working dir (alembic runs from backend/, so a
# CWD-relative dotenv lookup wouldn't find the root file).
step "Preparing .env / .env.app"
# Local-dev DB credentials are GENERATED here, never shipped in the tracked
# templates (those ship blank — we don't commit credentials, even mock ones).
# The password must match across both files: .env's POSTGRES_PASSWORD (the
# postgres container + the compose-built container DATABASE_URL) and .env.app's
# host-side DATABASE_URL (alembic/seed/uvicorn). user/db are non-secret
# identifiers; only the password is generated.
local_pg_user="dataq"
local_pg_db="dataq"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# One-command dev environment setup from a fresh clone.
# Usage: ./scripts/setup.sh
# Requires: conda (miniconda/miniforge), docker, pnpm, git

set -euo pipefail

CYAN='\033[0;36m'; GREEN='\033[0;32m'; RED='\033[0;31m'; NC='\033[0m'
step() { echo -e "${CYAN}▶ $1${NC}"; }
ok()   { echo -e "${GREEN}✓ $1${NC}"; }
die()  { echo -e "${RED}✗ $1${NC}" >&2; exit 1; }

# ── Prerequisites ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Checking prerequisites"
command -v conda  >/dev/null || die "conda not found — install miniconda or miniforge first"
command -v docker >/dev/null || die "docker not found"
command -v pnpm   >/dev/null || die "pnpm not found — run: npm install -g pnpm"
command -v git    >/dev/null || die "git not found"
ok "Prerequisites OK"

# ── Local env files ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Two files (split in #209 so Settings can run extra="forbid"):
#   .env     — infra/compose only (POSTGRES_*, VITE_*); compose substitutes ${...}
#              from it and the postgres service reads it.
#   .env.app — app config (DATABASE_URL, AZURE_*, …); the file Settings reads.
# App code carries no DB credentials (config.py default is credential-less), so
# host-side tooling (alembic, seed, uvicorn) needs DATABASE_URL from .env.app.
# Create both from their templates on first run, then export so child processes
# inherit them regardless of working dir (alembic runs from backend/, so a
# CWD-relative dotenv lookup wouldn't find the root file).
step "Preparing .env / .env.app"
# Local-dev DB credentials are GENERATED here, never shipped in the tracked
# templates (those ship blank — we don't commit credentials, even mock ones).
# The password must match across both files: .env's POSTGRES_PASSWORD (the
# postgres container + the compose-built container DATABASE_URL) and .env.app's
# host-side DATABASE_URL (alembic/seed/uvicorn). user/db are non-secret
# identifiers; only the password is generated.
local_pg_user="dataq"
local_pg_db="dataq"
# Reuse a password already set in .env (so re-runs stay consistent); otherwise
# generate a fresh hex one (URL-safe — no special chars to encode in
# DATABASE_URL). `=..*` matches only a NON-blank value, so a blank line doesn't
# count as "set".
local_pg_password="REDACTED"
if [ -z "${local_pg_password}" ]; then
  local_pg_password="REDACTED"
fi

# Same story for the OpenBao dev-mode root token (ADR 0039), except it must match
# across .env (compose starts the vault with it) AND .env.app (the app authenticates
# with it) — a mismatch 403s every credential read. Reuse whichever file already has
# one so re-runs stay consistent.
local_bao_token="$(sed -n 's/^OPENBAO_TOKEN=\(..*\)$/\1/p' .env 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
if [ -z "${local_bao_token}" ]; then
  local_bao_token="$(sed -n 's/^OPENBAO_TOKEN=\(..*\)$/\1/p' .env.app 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
fi
if [ -z "${local_bao_token}" ]; then
  local_bao_token="$(openssl rand -hex 16 2>/dev/null || date +%s | shasum | cut -c1-32)"
fi

# Create each file from its template if missing, then BACK-FILL the local-dev
# creds whenever the key is still blank — covers a fresh copy AND a pre-existing
# file left blank (e.g. a manual `cp` of the now-blank template). Without the
# back-fill, a blank POSTGRES_PASSWORD trips compose's `${VAR:?}` guard / mismatches
# the host DATABASE_URL.
[ -f .env ] || { cp .env.example .env; ok ".env created from .env.example"; }
if ! grep -qE '^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REDACTED .env; then
  sed -i.bak \
    -e "s|^POSTGRES_USER=.*|POSTGRES_USER=${local_pg_user}|" \
    -e "s|^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REDACTED \
    -e "s|^POSTGRES_DB=.*|POSTGRES_DB=${local_pg_db}|" .env && rm -f .env.bak
  ok ".env local Postgres creds generated"
fi

[ -f .env.app ] || { cp .env.app.example .env.app; ok ".env.app created from .env.app.example"; }
if ! grep -qE '^DATABASE_URL=..*$' .env.app; then
  db_url="REDACTED"
  sed -i.bak -e "s|^DATABASE_URL=.*|DATABASE_URL=${db_url}|" .env.app && rm -f .env.app.bak
  ok ".env.app host DATABASE_URL set"
fi
set -a
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. ./.env
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. ./.env.app
set +a

# ── Conda environment ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Creating / updating conda environment 'dataq'"
if conda env list | grep -q "^dataq "; then
  conda env update -n dataq -f environment.yml --prune
  ok "Conda env updated"
else
  conda env create -f environment.yml
  ok "Conda env created"
fi

# ── Pre-commit hooks ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# First run compiles the betterleaks secret-scanning hook (language: golang); this
# can take a minute. pre-commit (≥3.0) bootstraps its own Go — no system Go needed.
step "Installing pre-commit hooks"
conda run -n dataq pre-commit install --install-hooks
ok "Pre-commit hooks installed"

# ── Frontend dependencies ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Installing frontend dependencies (pnpm)"
(cd frontend && pnpm install)
ok "Frontend dependencies installed"

# ── Docker services ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Starting Docker services (Postgres, Redis)"
docker compose up -d postgres redis
ok "Docker services started"

# ── Database migrations ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Waiting for Postgres to be ready"
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  if docker compose exec -T postgres pg_isready -U dataq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ok "Postgres ready"
    break
  fi
  [ "$i" -eq 30 ] && die "Postgres did not become ready in time"
  sleep 1
done

step "Running Alembic migrations"
conda run -n dataq sh -c "cd backend && alembic upgrade head"
ok "Migrations applied"

# ── Seed data ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Run as a module (-m) so the repo root is on sys.path and `backend.*` imports
# resolve; running the file directly would not put the root on the path.
step "Seeding dev data"
conda run -n dataq python -m backend.scripts.seed_dev
ok "Dev data seeded"

# ── Done ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo ""
echo -e "${GREEN}━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━${NC}"

echo ""
echo "  Next steps:"
echo "    conda activate dataq"
echo "    docker compose up          # start all services"
echo "    # API: http://localhost:8000/docs"
echo "    # UI:  http://localhost:3000"
echo ""

=== README quickstart ===
## Quick start

### Run DataQ — prebuilt images (recommended)

Evaluate or self-host in ~5 minutes: **no source checkout, no Azure tenant.** Just Docker.

```bash
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/main/docker-compose.ghcr.yml
docker compose -f docker-compose.ghcr.yml up
```

Open **<http://localhost:3000>** — the stack comes up migrated and seeded with demo data, on **dev-bypass auth** (every request is a fixed demo user; no sign-in). API + Swagger at `http://localhost:8000/docs`. Images are pulled from GHCR and are **multi-arch** (amd64 + arm64), so Apple-Silicon runs native. Ports bind to `127.0.0.1` only. To pin a release instead of the moving tags: `DATAQ_BACKEND_TAG=vX.Y.Z DATAQ_FRONTEND_TAG=vX.Y.Z docker compose -f docker-compose.ghcr.yml up`.

> Self-hosting with **your own** Azure AD? The published frontend is **one generic image** — the compose eval runs it with `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass` (auth off). For real SSO, **no rebuild**: run that same image with `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=oidc` + `DATAQ_AUTH_AUTHORITY` / `DATAQ_AUTH_CLIENT_ID` / `DATAQ_AUTH_API_SCOPE` (auth config is injected at runtime, ADR 0028), and run the backend with `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS` off. See [Getting started](https://theurgicduke771.github.io/DataQ/getting-started/).

- name: Run migrations + seed demo data
        # alembic.ini's script_location is relative to backend/ (compose parity).

          (cd backend && alembic upgrade head)

      - name: Launch the API
        # Background uvicorn, then block until it serves before Playwright starts.
        run: |
          uvicorn backend.app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 &
          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
            if curl -sf http://localhost:8000/api/v1/connections >/dev/null; then
              echo "api up"; exit 0
            fi
            sleep 2
          done
          echo "api did not come up"; exit 1

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
        with:
          version: 9

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "24"

      - name: Install frontend
        working-directory: frontend
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Install Playwright browser
        working-directory: frontend
        # Split the browser download from its OS deps (#704). The Chromium binary
        # comes from the Playwright CDN (reliable). The `--with-deps` apt step used
        # to fail intermittently on the runner's pre-configured
        # packages.microsoft.com sources (azure-cli / MS-prod) — which DataQ's E2E
        # doesn't need — so drop those sources before apt runs, then install the OS
        # libs (from the standard Ubuntu archive) with a short retry as insurance.
        run: |
          pnpm exec playwright install chromium
          sudo rm -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*microsoft* /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*azure* || true
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if pnpm exec playwright install-deps chromium; then ok=1; break; fi
            echo "playwright install-deps attempt $attempt failed; retrying in 5s…"; sleep 5
          done
          [ -n "${ok:-}" ] || { echo "playwright install-deps failed after 3 attempts"; exit 1; }

      - name: Playwright E2E
        working-directory: frontend
        # CI=true → Playwright starts its own Vite dev server (proxying to the
        # api on :8000) and applies forbidOnly + flaky-retries.
        env:

        run: pnpm e2e

      - name: Upload Playwright report
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: playwright-report

import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path(".github/workflows/ci.yml"); s = p.read_text()

s = s.replace('''      # api + seed must share the secret store so secrets the seed writes are
      # readable by the api (compose parity). dev-bypass removes the auth wall.
      SECRET_STORE: redis''',
'''      # api + seed must share the secret store so secrets the seed writes are
      # readable by the api (compose parity) — EnvSecretStore is per-process and
      # they are separate processes here. dev-bypass removes the auth wall.
      # OPENBAO_TOKEN is generated per-run into $GITHUB_ENV by the step below:
      # no credential, not even a throwaway CI one, lives in a tracked file.
      SECRET_STORE: openbao
      OPENBAO_ADDR: http://localhost:8200''')

anchor = '''      - name: Run migrations + seed demo data'''
step = '''      - name: Start OpenBao (secret store)
        # A step rather than a `services:` container because the root token is
        # generated per run — service containers start before any step, so their
        # env cannot come from $GITHUB_ENV, and the alternative (a literal token
        # in this file) is exactly what CLAUDE.md §11 forbids. Dev mode is
        # in-memory and auto-unsealed, which is all a single CI run needs.
        run: |
          token="$(openssl rand -hex 16)"
          echo "::add-mask::$token"
          echo "OPENBAO_TOKEN=$token" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          docker run -d --name openbao -p 8200:8200 \\
            -e BAO_DEV_ROOT_TOKEN_ID="$token" \\
            -e BAO_DEV_LISTEN_ADDRESS="0.0.0.0:8200" \\
            --cap-add IPC_LOCK openbao/openbao:2.6.1
          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
            if curl -sf -o /dev/null http://localhost:8200/v1/sys/health; then
              echo "openbao up"; exit 0
            fi
            sleep 2
          done
          echo "openbao did not come up"; docker logs openbao; exit 1

'''
assert anchor in s
s = s.replace(anchor, step + anchor, 1)
p.write_text(s); print("ci patched")

# One-command dev environment setup from a fresh clone.

CYAN='\033[0;36m'; GREEN='\033[0;32m'; RED='\033[0;31m'; NC='\033[0m'
step() { echo -e "${CYAN}▶ $1${NC}"; }
ok()   { echo -e "${GREEN}✓ $1${NC}"; }
die()  { echo -e "${RED}✗ $1${NC}" >&2; exit 1; }

# ── Prerequisites ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Checking prerequisites"
command -v conda  >/dev/null || die "conda not found — install miniconda or miniforge first"
command -v docker >/dev/null || die "docker not found"
command -v pnpm   >/dev/null || die "pnpm not found — run: npm install -g pnpm"
command -v git    >/dev/null || die "git not found"
ok "Prerequisites OK"

# ── Local env files ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Two files (split in #209 so Settings can run extra="forbid"):
#   .env     — infra/compose only (POSTGRES_*, VITE_*); compose substitutes ${...}
#              from it and the postgres service reads it.
#   .env.app — app config (DATABASE_URL, AZURE_*, …); the file Settings reads.
# App code carries no DB credentials (config.py default is credential-less), so
# host-side tooling (alembic, seed, uvicorn) needs DATABASE_URL from .env.app.
# Create both from their templates on first run, then export so child processes
# inherit them regardless of working dir (alembic runs from backend/, so a
# CWD-relative dotenv lookup wouldn't find the root file).
step "Preparing .env / .env.app"
# Local-dev DB credentials are GENERATED here, never shipped in the tracked
# templates (those ship blank — we don't commit credentials, even mock ones).
# The password must match across both files: .env's POSTGRES_PASSWORD (the
# postgres container + the compose-built container DATABASE_URL) and .env.app's
# host-side DATABASE_URL (alembic/seed/uvicorn). user/db are non-secret
# identifiers; only the password is generated.
local_pg_user="dataq"
local_pg_db="dataq"
# Reuse a password already set in .env (so re-runs stay consistent); otherwise
# generate a fresh hex one (URL-safe — no special chars to encode in
# DATABASE_URL). `=..*` matches only a NON-blank value, so a blank line doesn't
# count as "set".
local_pg_password="REDACTED"
if [ -z "${local_pg_password}" ]; then
  local_pg_password="REDACTED"
fi

# Same story for the OpenBao dev-mode root token (ADR 0039), except it must match
# across .env (compose starts the vault with it) AND .env.app (the app authenticates
# with it) — a mismatch 403s every credential read. Reuse whichever file already has
# one so re-runs stay consistent.
local_bao_token="$(sed -n 's/^OPENBAO_TOKEN=\(..*\)$/\1/p' .env 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
if [ -z "${local_bao_token}" ]; then
  local_bao_token="$(sed -n 's/^OPENBAO_TOKEN=\(..*\)$/\1/p' .env.app 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
fi
if [ -z "${local_bao_token}" ]; then
  local_bao_token="$(openssl rand -hex 16 2>/dev/null || date +%s | shasum | cut -c1-32)"
fi

# creds whenever the key is still blank — covers a fresh copy AND a pre-existing
# file left blank (e.g. a manual `cp` of the now-blank template). Without the
# back-fill, a blank POSTGRES_PASSWORD trips compose's `${VAR:?}` guard / mismatches
# the host DATABASE_URL.
[ -f .env ] || { cp .env.example .env; ok ".env created from .env.example"; }
if ! grep -qE '^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REDACTED .env; then
  sed -i.bak \
    -e "s|^POSTGRES_USER=.*|POSTGRES_USER=${local_pg_user}|" \
    -e "s|^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REDACTED \
    -e "s|^POSTGRES_DB=.*|POSTGRES_DB=${local_pg_db}|" .env && rm -f .env.bak
  ok ".env local Postgres creds generated"
fi
if ! grep -qE '^OPENBAO_TOKEN=..*$' .env; then
  sed -i.bak -e "s|^OPENBAO_TOKEN=.*|OPENBAO_TOKEN=${local_bao_token}|" .env && rm -f .env.bak

fi

[ -f .env.app ] || { cp .env.app.example .env.app; ok ".env.app created from .env.app.example"; }
if ! grep -qE '^DATABASE_URL=..*$' .env.app; then
  db_url="REDACTED"
  sed -i.bak -e "s|^DATABASE_URL=.*|DATABASE_URL=${db_url}|" .env.app && rm -f .env.app.bak

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# One-command dev environment setup from a fresh clone.
# Usage: ./scripts/setup.sh
# Requires: conda (miniconda/miniforge), docker, pnpm, git

set -euo pipefail

CYAN='\033[0;36m'; GREEN='\033[0;32m'; RED='\033[0;31m'; NC='\033[0m'
step() { echo -e "${CYAN}▶ $1${NC}"; }
ok()   { echo -e "${GREEN}✓ $1${NC}"; }
die()  { echo -e "${RED}✗ $1${NC}" >&2; exit 1; }

# set_env_kv <file> <key> <value> — set KEY=value, leaving an already-non-blank
# value alone. Substitutes when the key is present (blank or not) and APPENDS when
# it is absent: a plain `sed s|^KEY=.*|` is a silent no-op on a .env that predates
# the key, which would leave the file short of a value compose then refuses to
# start without — telling the user to run this script, which they just did.
set_env_kv() {
  local file="$1" key="$2" value="$3"
  grep -qE "^${key}=..*$" "${file}" && return 0        # already set — keep it
  if grep -qE "^${key}=" "${file}"; then
    sed -i.bak -e "s|^${key}=.*|${key}=${value}|" "${file}" && rm -f "${file}.bak"
  else
    printf '%s=%s\n' "${key}" "${value}" >> "${file}"
  fi
}

# ── Prerequisites ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Checking prerequisites"
command -v conda  >/dev/null || die "conda not found — install miniconda or miniforge first"
command -v docker >/dev/null || die "docker not found"
command -v pnpm   >/dev/null || die "pnpm not found — run: npm install -g pnpm"
command -v git    >/dev/null || die "git not found"
ok "Prerequisites OK"

# ── Local env files ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Two files (split in #209 so Settings can run extra="forbid"):
#   .env     — infra/compose only (POSTGRES_*, VITE_*); compose substitutes ${...}
#              from it and the postgres service reads it.
#   .env.app — app config (DATABASE_URL, AZURE_*, …); the file Settings reads.
# App code carries no DB credentials (config.py default is credential-less), so
# host-side tooling (alembic, seed, uvicorn) needs DATABASE_URL from .env.app.
# Create both from their templates on first run, then export so child processes
# inherit them regardless of working dir (alembic runs from backend/, so a
# CWD-relative dotenv lookup wouldn't find the root file).
step "Preparing .env / .env.app"
# Local-dev DB credentials are GENERATED here, never shipped in the tracked
# templates (those ship blank — we don't commit credentials, even mock ones).
# The password must match across both files: .env's POSTGRES_PASSWORD (the
# postgres container + the compose-built container DATABASE_URL) and .env.app's
# host-side DATABASE_URL (alembic/seed/uvicorn). user/db are non-secret
# identifiers; only the password is generated.
local_pg_user="dataq"
local_pg_db="dataq"
# Reuse a password already set in .env (so re-runs stay consistent); otherwise
# generate a fresh hex one (URL-safe — no special chars to encode in
# DATABASE_URL). `=..*` matches only a NON-blank value, so a blank line doesn't
# count as "set".
local_pg_password="REDACTED"
if [ -z "${local_pg_password}" ]; then
  local_pg_password="REDACTED"
fi

# Same story for the OpenBao dev-mode root token (ADR 0039), except it must match

# with it) — a mismatch 403s every credential read. Reuse whichever file already has

fi

fi

  sed -i.bak \
    -e "s|^POSTGRES_USER=.*|POSTGRES_USER=${local_pg_user}|" \
    -e "s|^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REDACTED \
    -e "s|^POSTGRES_DB=.*|POSTGRES_DB=${local_pg_db}|" .env && rm -f .env.bak
  ok ".env local Postgres creds generated"
fi
if ! grep -qE '^OPENBAO_TOKEN=..*$' .env; then
  sed -i.bak -e "s|^OPENBAO_TOKEN=.*|OPENBAO_TOKEN=${local_bao_token}|" .env && rm -f .env.bak
  ok ".env OpenBao dev root token generated"
fi

fi

  sed -i.bak -e "s|^OPENBAO_TOKEN=.*|OPENBAO_TOKEN=${local_bao_token}|" .env.app && rm -f .env.app.bak

fi
set -a
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. ./.env
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. ./.env.app
set +a

# ── Conda environment ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Creating / updating conda environment 'dataq'"
if conda env list | grep -q "^dataq "; then
  conda env update -n dataq -f environment.yml --prune
  ok "Conda env updated"
else
  conda env create -f environment.yml
  ok "Conda env created"
fi

# ── Pre-commit hooks ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# First run compiles the betterleaks secret-scanning hook (language: golang); this
# can take a minute. pre-commit (≥3.0) bootstraps its own Go — no system Go needed.
step "Installing pre-commit hooks"
conda run -n dataq pre-commit install --install-hooks
ok "Pre-commit hooks installed"

# ── Frontend dependencies ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Installing frontend dependencies (pnpm)"
(cd frontend && pnpm install)
ok "Frontend dependencies installed"

# ── Docker services ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Starting Docker services (Postgres, Redis)"
docker compose up -d postgres redis
ok "Docker services started"

# ── Database migrations ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Waiting for Postgres to be ready"
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  if docker compose exec -T postgres pg_isready -U dataq >/dev/null 2>&1; then

step "Seeding dev data"
conda run -n dataq python -m backend.scripts.seed_dev

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# One-command dev environment setup from a fresh clone.
# Usage: ./scripts/setup.sh
# Requires: conda (miniconda/miniforge), docker, pnpm, git

set -euo pipefail

CYAN='\033[0;36m'; GREEN='\033[0;32m'; RED='\033[0;31m'; NC='\033[0m'
step() { echo -e "${CYAN}▶ $1${NC}"; }
ok()   { echo -e "${GREEN}✓ $1${NC}"; }
die()  { echo -e "${RED}✗ $1${NC}" >&2; exit 1; }

# set_env_kv <file> <key> <value> — set KEY=value, leaving an already-non-blank
# value alone. Substitutes when the key is present (blank or not) and APPENDS when
# it is absent: a plain `sed s|^KEY=.*|` is a silent no-op on a .env that predates
# the key, which would leave the file short of a value compose then refuses to
# start without — telling the user to run this script, which they just did.
set_env_kv() {
  local file="$1" key="$2" value="$3"
  grep -qE "^${key}=..*$" "${file}" && return 0        # already set — keep it
  if grep -qE "^${key}=" "${file}"; then
    sed -i.bak -e "s|^${key}=.*|${key}=${value}|" "${file}" && rm -f "${file}.bak"
  else
    printf '%s=%s\n' "${key}" "${value}" >> "${file}"
  fi
}

# ── Prerequisites ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Checking prerequisites"
command -v conda  >/dev/null || die "conda not found — install miniconda or miniforge first"
command -v docker >/dev/null || die "docker not found"
command -v pnpm   >/dev/null || die "pnpm not found — run: npm install -g pnpm"
command -v git    >/dev/null || die "git not found"
ok "Prerequisites OK"

# ── Local env files ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Two files (split in #209 so Settings can run extra="forbid"):
#   .env     — infra/compose only (POSTGRES_*, VITE_*); compose substitutes ${...}
#              from it and the postgres service reads it.
#   .env.app — app config (DATABASE_URL, AZURE_*, …); the file Settings reads.
# App code carries no DB credentials (config.py default is credential-less), so
# host-side tooling (alembic, seed, uvicorn) needs DATABASE_URL from .env.app.
# Create both from their templates on first run, then export so child processes
# inherit them regardless of working dir (alembic runs from backend/, so a
# CWD-relative dotenv lookup wouldn't find the root file).
step "Preparing .env / .env.app"
# Local-dev DB credentials are GENERATED here, never shipped in the tracked
# templates (those ship blank — we don't commit credentials, even mock ones).
# The password must match across both files: .env's POSTGRES_PASSWORD (the
# postgres container + the compose-built container DATABASE_URL) and .env.app's
# host-side DATABASE_URL (alembic/seed/uvicorn). user/db are non-secret
# identifiers; only the password is generated.
local_pg_user="dataq"
local_pg_db="dataq"
# Reuse a password already set in .env (so re-runs stay consistent); otherwise
# generate a fresh hex one (URL-safe — no special chars to encode in
# DATABASE_URL). `=..*` matches only a NON-blank value, so a blank line doesn't
# count as "set".
local_pg_password="REDACTED"
if [ -z "${local_pg_password}" ]; then
  local_pg_password="REDACTED"
fi

# Same story for the OpenBao dev-mode root token (ADR 0039), except it must match
# across .env (compose starts the vault with it) AND .env.app (the app authenticates
# with it) — a mismatch 403s every credential read. Reuse whichever file already has
# one so re-runs stay consistent.
local_bao_token="$(sed -n 's/^OPENBAO_TOKEN=\(..*\)$/\1/p' .env 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
if [ -z "${local_bao_token}" ]; then
  local_bao_token="$(sed -n 's/^OPENBAO_TOKEN=\(..*\)$/\1/p' .env.app 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
fi
if [ -z "${local_bao_token}" ]; then
  local_bao_token="$(openssl rand -hex 16 2>/dev/null || date +%s | shasum | cut -c1-32)"
fi

# Create each file from its template if missing, then BACK-FILL the local-dev
# creds whenever the key is still blank — covers a fresh copy AND a pre-existing
# file left blank (e.g. a manual `cp` of the now-blank template). Without the
# back-fill, a blank POSTGRES_PASSWORD trips compose's `${VAR:?}` guard / mismatches
# the host DATABASE_URL.
[ -f .env ] || { cp .env.example .env; ok ".env created from .env.example"; }
if ! grep -qE '^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REDACTED .env; then
  sed -i.bak \
    -e "s|^POSTGRES_USER=.*|POSTGRES_USER=${local_pg_user}|" \
    -e "s|^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REDACTED \
    -e "s|^POSTGRES_DB=.*|POSTGRES_DB=${local_pg_db}|" .env && rm -f .env.bak
  ok ".env local Postgres creds generated"
fi
if ! grep -qE '^OPENBAO_TOKEN=..*$' .env; then
  set_env_kv .env OPENBAO_TOKEN "${local_bao_token}"
  ok ".env OpenBao dev root token generated"
fi

[ -f .env.app ] || { cp .env.app.example .env.app; ok ".env.app created from .env.app.example"; }
if ! grep -qE '^DATABASE_URL=..*$' .env.app; then
  db_url="REDACTED"
  sed -i.bak -e "s|^DATABASE_URL=.*|DATABASE_URL=${db_url}|" .env.app && rm -f .env.app.bak
  ok ".env.app host DATABASE_URL set"
fi
if ! grep -qE '^OPENBAO_TOKEN=..*$' .env.app; then
  set_env_kv .env.app OPENBAO_TOKEN "${local_bao_token}"
  ok ".env.app OpenBao token set (matches .env)"
fi
# Host-side dev (uvicorn/celery on your machine) reads these from .env.app; the
# compose api/worker override the address to the in-network hostname. Appended for
# a .env.app that predates ADR 0039 so a re-run leaves a complete file. SECRET_STORE
# is deliberately NOT rewritten — an existing `redis` value raises at startup with
# the migration path, and silently changing someone's configured mode is worse.
set_env_kv .env.app OPENBAO_ADDR "http://localhost:8200"
set_env_kv .env.app OPENBAO_MOUNT "secret"
set -a
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. ./.env
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. ./.env.app
set +a

# ── Conda environment ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Creating / updating conda environment 'dataq'"
if conda env list | grep -q "^dataq "; then
  conda env update -n dataq -f environment.yml --prune
  ok "Conda env updated"
else
  conda env create -f environment.yml
  ok "Conda env created"
fi

# ── Pre-commit hooks ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# First run compiles the betterleaks secret-scanning hook (language: golang); this
# can take a minute. pre-commit (≥3.0) bootstraps its own Go — no system Go needed.
step "Installing pre-commit hooks"
conda run -n dataq pre-commit install --install-hooks
ok "Pre-commit hooks installed"

# ── Frontend dependencies ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Installing frontend dependencies (pnpm)"
(cd frontend && pnpm install)
ok "Frontend dependencies installed"

# ── Docker services ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Starting Docker services (Postgres, Redis)"
docker compose up -d postgres redis
ok "Docker services started"

# ── Database migrations ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Waiting for Postgres to be ready"
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  if docker compose exec -T postgres pg_isready -U dataq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ok "Postgres ready"
    break
  fi
  [ "$i" -eq 30 ] && die "Postgres did not become ready in time"
  sleep 1
done

step "Running Alembic migrations"
conda run -n dataq sh -c "cd backend && alembic upgrade head"
ok "Migrations applied"

# ── Seed data ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Run as a module (-m) so the repo root is on sys.path and `backend.*` imports
# resolve; running the file directly would not put the root on the path.
step "Seeding dev data"
conda run -n dataq python -m backend.scripts.seed_dev
ok "Dev data seeded"

# ── Done ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo ""
echo -e "${GREEN}━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━${NC}"
echo -e "${GREEN}  DataQ dev environment ready!${NC}"
echo -e "${GREEN}━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━${NC}"
echo ""
echo "  Next steps:"
echo "    conda activate dataq"
echo "    docker compose up          # start all services"
echo "    # API: http://localhost:8000/docs"
echo "    # UI:  http://localhost:3000"
echo ""

**4. Token auth only in phase 1.** `OPENBAO_TOKEN` is sent as `X-Vault-Token`. AppRole (`role_id`/`secret_id` → login → renewable token), which is what a production self-hosted deployment should use, is **deferred and filed**, not silently omitted — see Related. The token is never logged: it is not in the request path or query string, and the logger-level redactor (ADR-independent, `backend/app/core/logging.py`) covers `token` keys and bare token shapes. No credential enters a git-tracked file — `scripts/setup.sh` generates the local dev-mode root token into the gitignored `.env`, exactly as it already does for the local Postgres password (CLAUDE.md §11).

**5. Azure Key Vault remains the production default for DataQ's own Azure deployment.** Managed identity means no bootstrap credential at all, which is strictly better than a token DataQ has to hold, and the Terraform stack (ADR 0024) already provisions it. OpenBao is the **cloud-neutral option for BYOL deployments**, not a replacement for Key Vault on Azure. One store implementation covering AWS + GCP + on-prem beats building and maintaining AWS Secrets Manager and GCP Secret Manager adapters separately.

content.text: Root cause: once `configure_logging()` runs (an earlier test does it), structlog caches the bound logger on first use, and a cached logger bypasses `capture_logs`'s processors — so the assertion silently sees zero events. Fixing both failures:

input.command:
python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path("backend/tests/core/test_secrets.py"); s = p.read_text()

s = s.replace('''def _events(logs: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]]) -> list[str]:
    """Event names captured by structlog, in order. `capture_logs` is used rather
    than `caplog` because the stdlib bridge is only installed by `configure_logging`
    at app startup, which a bare unit test never runs — asserting on `caplog.text`
    silently passes an empty string."""
    return [str(entry["event"]) for entry in logs]''',
'''def _events(logs: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]]) -> list[str]:
    """Event names captured by structlog, in order. `capture_logs` is used rather
    than `caplog` because the stdlib bridge is only installed by `configure_logging`
    at app startup, which a bare unit test never runs — asserting on `caplog.text`
    silently passes an empty string."""
    return [str(entry["event"]) for entry in logs]


@contextmanager
def _captured_secret_logs(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> Iterator[list[EventDict]]:
    """`capture_logs`, with the module logger rebound INSIDE the capture.

    Necessary because `configure_logging()` sets `cache_logger_on_first_use=True`,
    and once some earlier test in the suite has run it, `secrets.log` caches its
    bound logger and bypasses the processors `capture_logs` installs. The capture
    then yields an EMPTY list and every assertion here passes vacuously — these
    tests were green in isolation and failed only in the full suite, which is the
    same "passes for the wrong reason" shape the project keeps hitting.
    """
    with capture_logs() as logs:
        monkeypatch.setattr(secrets, "log", structlog.get_logger("backend.app.core.secrets"))
        yield logs''')

s = s.replace('''import httpx
import pytest
from structlog.testing import capture_logs''',
'''import httpx
import pytest
import structlog
from structlog.testing import EventDict, capture_logs''')
s = s.replace('''from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping, Sequence''',
'''from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator, Mapping, Sequence
from contextlib import contextmanager''')

# Rewrite the six log tests onto the robust helper.
pairs = [
    ('''def test_openbao_get_403_logs_a_warning() -> None:
    """The exception reaches the caller, but only a LOG reaches the operator."""
    store = _bao(lambda _r: httpx.Response(403, json={"errors": ["permission denied"]}))
    with capture_logs() as logs, pytest.raises(SecretNotFoundError):
        store.get("conn-1")
    assert _events(logs) == ["openbao_permission_denied"]''',
     '''def test_openbao_get_403_logs_a_warning(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    """The exception reaches the caller, but only a LOG reaches the operator."""
    store = _bao(lambda _r: httpx.Response(403, json={"errors": ["permission denied"]}))
    with _captured_secret_logs(monkeypatch) as logs, pytest.raises(SecretNotFoundError):
        store.get("conn-1")
    assert _events(logs) == ["openbao_permission_denied"]'''),
    ('''def test_openbao_get_503_logs_unreachable() -> None:
    store = _bao(lambda _r: httpx.Response(503, json={"errors": ["Vault is sealed"]}))
    with capture_logs() as logs, pytest.raises(SecretNotFoundError):
        store.get("conn-1")
    assert _events(logs) == ["openbao_unreachable"]''',
     '''def test_openbao_get_503_logs_unreachable(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    store = _bao(lambda _r: httpx.Response(503, json={"errors": ["Vault is sealed"]}))
    with _captured_secret_logs(monkeypatch) as logs, pytest.raises(SecretNotFoundError):
        store.get("conn-1")
    assert _events(logs) == ["openbao_unreachable"]'''),
    ('''def test_openbao_get_transport_error_logs_unreachable() -> None:
    def handler(_request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        raise httpx.ConnectError("connection refused")

    with capture_logs() as logs, pytest.raises(SecretNotFoundError):
        _bao(handler).get("conn-1")
    assert _events(logs) == ["openbao_unreachable"]''',
     '''def test_openbao_get_transport_error_logs_unreachable(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    def handler(_request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        raise httpx.ConnectError("connection refused")

    with _captured_secret_logs(monkeypatch) as logs, pytest.raises(SecretNotFoundError):
        _bao(handler).get("conn-1")
    assert _events(logs) == ["openbao_unreachable"]'''),
    ('''def test_openbao_delete_of_absent_secret_is_a_clean_noop() -> None:
    """KV v2 answers 204 even for a name that never existed — nothing to log."""
    store = _bao(lambda _r: httpx.Response(204))
    with capture_logs() as logs:
        store.delete("never-existed")
    assert _events(logs) == []''',
     '''def test_openbao_delete_of_absent_secret_is_a_clean_noop(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """KV v2 answers 204 even for a name that never existed — nothing to log."""
    store = _bao(lambda _r: httpx.Response(204))
    with _captured_secret_logs(monkeypatch) as logs:
        store.delete("never-existed")
    assert _events(logs) == []'''),
    ('''def test_openbao_delete_fails_soft_on_transport_error() -> None:
    def handler(_request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        raise httpx.ConnectError("connection refused")

    with capture_logs() as logs:
        _bao(handler).delete("conn-1")  # fail-soft: logged, never raised (#372)
    assert _events(logs) == ["secret_delete_failed"]''',
     '''def test_openbao_delete_fails_soft_on_transport_error(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    def handler(_request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        raise httpx.ConnectError("connection refused")

    with _captured_secret_logs(monkeypatch) as logs:
        _bao(handler).delete("conn-1")  # fail-soft: logged, never raised (#372)
    assert _events(logs) == ["secret_delete_failed"]'''),
    ('''def test_openbao_delete_fails_soft_on_error_status() -> None:
    store = _bao(lambda _r: httpx.Response(403, json={"errors": ["permission denied"]}))
    with capture_logs() as logs:
        store.delete("conn-1")  # fail-soft: an entity delete must not 500 on this
    assert _events(logs) == ["secret_delete_failed"]''',
     '''def test_openbao_delete_fails_soft_on_error_status(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    store = _bao(lambda _r: httpx.Response(403, json={"errors": ["permission denied"]}))
    with _captured_secret_logs(monkeypatch) as logs:
        store.delete("conn-1")  # fail-soft: an entity delete must not 500 on this
    assert _events(logs) == ["secret_delete_failed"]'''),
]
for old, new in pairs:
    assert old in s, old[:60]
    s = s.replace(old, new)
p.write_text(s); print("test_secrets patched")

# ── the local-first posture tests encode the OLD default ──
p = pathlib.Path("backend/tests/core/test_local_first_posture.py"); s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace('''    assert values["SECRET_STORE"] == "redis"  # not azure_key_vault''',
'''    assert values["SECRET_STORE"] == "openbao"  # local vault in compose, not azure_key_vault''')
s = s.replace('''    for key in (
        "AZURE_TENANT_ID",''',
'''    for key in (
        # A credential, so it ships blank and setup.sh generates it (ADR 0039).
        "OPENBAO_TOKEN",
        "AZURE_TENANT_ID",''')
s = s.replace('''    assert "SECRET_STORE=redis" in guide''', '''    assert "SECRET_STORE=openbao" in guide''')
p.write_text(s); print("posture test patched")
PYEOF

input.command:
gh pr create --title "feat(secrets): OpenBao as the self-hosted secret backend, replacing the plaintext Redis store (ADR 0039)" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What & why

Adds a fourth `SecretStore` backend speaking the **KV v2 HTTP API** and deletes `RedisSecretStore`, which kept warehouse credentials in **plaintext** — and was the configured default of `docker-compose.ghcr.yml`, the published eval stack. An evaluator following our own README was putting real credentials into an unencrypted, unauthenticated key-value store.

Records the decision as **ADR [0039](docs/adr/0039-openbao-self-hosted-secret-backend.md)**.

Two things this is *not*: it does not remove Redis (still the Celery broker + the ADR 0035 rate-limit counters — this drops one of its two unrelated jobs), and it does not change production on Azure (Key Vault stays the default there; managed identity beats a token we have to hold).

## The two decisions worth reviewing

**1. The contract is the API, not a vendor.** Three plain `httpx` calls, so the same mode serves OpenBao, Vault Community, Vault Enterprise and HCP. Trading Azure lock-in for HashiCorp lock-in would have missed the point of ADR 0010. `hvac` was rejected — a dependency and a vendor-shaped abstraction for three HTTP calls (revisit at AppRole time, #1054).

**2. OpenBao, not Vault Community.** Vault Community has been **BUSL-1.1 since 1.15**, which CONTRIBUTING rule 40 / ADR 0031 §4 forbid as a *distributed* component. OpenBao is the Linux Foundation fork at the pre-BUSL point, **MPL-2.0** — so no license exception is needed and nothing source-available enters the marketplace path (#732). Vault stays *supported as a target*, just never shipped by us.

## Failure modes stay distinguishable

`403` (dead token) and `503` (sealed) **never** report as "secret not set" — they log a WARNING and name the cause. This is written directly against #954, where two dead Snowflake PATs had no visible state anywhere and had to be root-caused from worker logs, and #828 more generally. A credential store that says "your credential is missing" when it means "I cannot reach the vault" is an invisible-degradation machine.

## Verification

The API surface and every response shape were **captured from `openbao/openbao` v2.6.1**, not taken from docs — including that a soft-deleted secret returns 404 like an absent one.

Live-verified in the running compose stack:
- credential written through the real API lands in KV v2 under the `value` field
- the **worker** (separate container) resolves what the **api** wrote — the #86 cross-process property the plaintext store existed to provide
- nothing written to Redis
- all three failure modes distinguishable in the running system (403 / 503 / genuinely-absent)
- the documented dev-mode caveat (restart drops credentials) confirmed rather than assumed

Tests drive a **real `httpx.Client` over `MockTransport`**, so URL building, header encoding, status handling and JSON decoding execute rather than get stubbed past. All mutants killed: collapsed statuses, `data/`-vs-`metadata` delete, dropped auth header, unquoted name, flattened KV envelope, null value, and removed operator warnings.

## Two defects the process caught

- **A test caught a design flaw**: the token was originally set on the pooled client, which meant an injected client silently carried no credential. Auth now travels per-request.
- **The log assertions passed vacuously.** Green alone, failing in the full suite: `configure_logging()` sets `cache_logger_on_first_use=True`, so a cached module logger bypasses `capture_logs` and the capture yields an empty list — which the `== []` assertions would have accepted forever. Fixed, then re-verified by removing the warnings and confirming failure in a **full-suite** run.

## Migration

`SECRET_STORE=redis` stays in the `Literal` for one cycle and raises with the migration path, rather than letting pydantic emit a bare "Input should be …" that names no cause. The live migration left **1392 `dataq:secret:*` plaintext keys** in Redis, so the error also carries the purge command — a migration away from plaintext storage that leaves the plaintext in place is half a fix.

No credential lands in a tracked file: `setup.sh` generates the dev root token into the gitignored `.env` and `.env.app`, and CI generates one per run in a **step** (service containers start before any step, so their env cannot come from `$GITHUB_ENV`).

## Checks

- [x] Full backend suite: **2755 passed**, coverage 97.26% (gate 80%)
- [x] black / ruff / mypy (295 files) / pre-commit clean
- [x] bandit unchanged from baseline (27 both sides — adds none)
- [x] both compose stacks validate; the missing-token guards verified by running `docker compose config` unset
- [x] Live-verified against a real vault

Fixes #1055. Refs #86, #372, #505. Deferred: AppRole auth #1054.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

content.text:
Both review agents and CI are running. Here's where things stand:

**Answering your original questions, now settled as decisions:**

- **OpenBao does not replace Redis.** Redis wore two unrelated hats; this removes one of them. It stays as the Celery broker, beat store, and rate-limit counter store. The local stack *gains* a container — it doesn't lose one.
- **Edition: OpenBao, and the code speaks the KV v2 API rather than a vendor SDK** — so the same mode serves Vault Community, Enterprise, or HCP for anyone already running them. That sidesteps the edition question entirely instead of answering it.

**What shipped (PR [#1056](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1056), 7 commits):**

ADR [0039](docs/adr/0039-openbao-self-hosted-secret-backend.md), the `OpenBaoSecretStore`, and wiring for the dev stack, the GHCR eval stack, and CI.

One thing worth flagging, because it changed the shape of the work: `RedisSecretStore` wasn't only a local-dev convenience. It was the configured default of `docker-compose.ghcr.yml` — the artifact the README tells strangers to run. Anyone evaluating DataQ was putting real warehouse credentials into an unencrypted, unauthenticated key-value store. That moved this from "nice cleanup" to fixing a live defect in the published artifact.

**Findings from verification, not from planning:**

- I probed a real OpenBao container before writing code. That surfaced the load-bearing detail: **403 (dead token) and 503 (sealed) are distinct from 404**. Collapsing them would have rebuilt the #954 blindness where dead PATs had no visible state. The store now names the cause and logs a warning for each.
- **A test caught a design flaw of mine** — I'd put the auth token on the pooled client, which meant an injected client silently carried no credential. Auth now travels per-request.
- **My log assertions were passing vacuously.** Green alone, failing in the full suite: `configure_logging()` enables logger caching, and a cached logger bypasses `capture_logs`, so the capture yielded an empty list that two `== []` assertions would have accepted forever. Found only because I ran the whole battery rather than the file I'd touched. Re-verified by removing the warnings and confirming failure in a *full-suite* run.
- **The live migration left 1392 plaintext credentials in Redis.** Switching modes deletes nothing. A migration away from plaintext that leaves the plaintext in place is half a fix, so the removal error carries the purge command.

**Live-verified end to end**, not just mocked: a credential written through the real API lands in KV v2, the **worker container reads what the api wrote** (the #86 property), nothing goes to Redis, and all three failure modes stay distinct in the running system.

**Two follow-ups filed:** AppRole auth [#1054](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1054) (token auth is phase 1 — weaker than managed identity, but it replaces *no auth at all*). And [#1055](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1055), a pre-existing bug I fixed here: `httpx` is imported by six runtime modules but was declared dev-only, reaching production transitively via `openlineage` — unpinned from our side.

One deliberate trade to confirm you're happy with: the eval stack now needs `export OPENBAO_TOKEN=$(openssl rand -hex 16)` before `docker compose up`. A vault has no "no auth" mode, and defaulting a token in a tracked file would break CLAUDE.md §11 — so the one-command promise loses one line. I'll report the review findings and CI result when they land.

content.text: Confirmed a real merge-ordering hazard: `publish-images.yml` runs only on manual dispatch or a `v*` tag — **not** on merge to main. But `README` tells evaluators to `curl` the compose file from `main`. So between merge and an image publish, the eval stack would set `SECRET_STORE=openbao` against a `:latest` image that doesn't know the mode.

input.command:
gh issue create --title "Merging #1056 breaks the GHCR eval stack until images are republished (compose-file/image version skew)" --label "bug" --milestone "v1.1 Week 5 — anomaly monitor kind + metric trends" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## The window

`docker-compose.ghcr.yml` and the published images are versioned **independently**:

- README / `docs/getting-started.md` tell evaluators to `curl` the compose file from **`main`**, so a merge is visible to users immediately.
- `.github/workflows/publish-images.yml` runs only on **`workflow_dispatch`** or a **`v*` tag push** — *not* on merge to `main`. `ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:latest` therefore does **not** move when a PR lands.

#1056 sets `SECRET_STORE: "openbao"` in that compose file. The currently-published `:latest` backend image validates `SECRET_STORE` against `Literal["env", "redis", "azure_key_vault"]`, so between merging #1056 and republishing images, the documented eval flow fails at startup with a pydantic error naming neither the cause nor a fix:

```
SECRET_STORE
  Input should be 'env', 'redis' or 'azure_key_vault'
```

That lands on exactly the artifact #1056 exists to make safer, and on the audience least equipped to debug it (a first-time evaluator with no source checkout).

## Fix

**Run `publish-images.yml` immediately after #1056 merges.** The new image accepts `openbao`, and compose + image are consistent again.

## Worth fixing properly

The skew is structural, not specific to this change: *any* PR touching `docker-compose.ghcr.yml` in a way that depends on new backend behaviour has the same window. Options:

1. Publish `:latest` on every merge to `main` (closes the window; costs a build per merge).
2. Have the eval compose pin a released tag rather than `:latest`, so the file and the image it names always match.
3. Keep it manual but add a PR-template checkbox: "touched `docker-compose.ghcr.yml`? → dispatch `publish-images` on merge".

(2) is the most honest — `:latest` floating against a `main`-tracked compose file is the actual defect — but it changes the "always get the newest" eval promise.

Found while verifying #1056; the `docker compose config` validation passes because the skew is a *runtime* mismatch, not a compose-syntax one.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

input.command: sed -n '140,175p' scripts/setup.sh
input.description: Check what services setup.sh starts before seeding

content.content:
(cd frontend && pnpm install)
ok "Frontend dependencies installed"

# ── Docker services ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Starting Docker services (Postgres, Redis)"
docker compose up -d postgres redis
ok "Docker services started"

# ── Database migrations ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Waiting for Postgres to be ready"
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  if docker compose exec -T postgres pg_isready -U dataq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ok "Postgres ready"
    break
  fi
  [ "$i" -eq 30 ] && die "Postgres did not become ready in time"
  sleep 1
done

step "Running Alembic migrations"
conda run -n dataq sh -c "cd backend && alembic upgrade head"
ok "Migrations applied"

# ── Seed data ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Run as a module (-m) so the repo root is on sys.path and `backend.*` imports
# resolve; running the file directly would not put the root on the path.
step "Seeding dev data"
conda run -n dataq python -m backend.scripts.seed_dev
ok "Dev data seeded"

# KV v2 stores a MAP per path; DataQ's model is one opaque string per name, so every
# value lives under one fixed field. Changing this orphans every existing secret.
_KV_FIELD: Final = "value"
# Bounded timeout (seconds) — a degraded vault must not stall a request thread or a
# Celery task. Mirrors marquez.py's `_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` rationale.
_HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: Final = 5.0


def _explain_status(status: int) -> str:
    """Turn a KV v2 status into a cause an operator can act on.

    The point is that these are NOT "secret missing" — see `OpenBaoSecretStore`.
    """
    if status == 403:
        return "permission denied — token invalid, expired, or lacking a policy for this path"
    if status == 503:
        return "vault sealed or standby — unseal it, or point OPENBAO_ADDR at the active node"
    return "unexpected vault response"

+    """Distinguish the two things KV v2 answers 404 to.
+    An absent (or soft-deleted) secret under a live mount returns an EMPTY error
+    list; a mount that does not exist returns a populated one::
+        mount not found → {"errors": ["no handler for route \\"typo/data/x\\". …"]}
+    Both shapes captured from openbao/openbao v2.6.1. The distinction matters
+    because `OPENBAO_MOUNT` is operator-settable and production vaults commonly
+    mount per-team paths: one typo would otherwise report EVERY credential in the
+    workspace as "not set" — the exact masquerade this class exists to prevent
+    (#954). A body we cannot parse is treated as the benign case, since only the
+    populated-errors shape is positive evidence of a bad route.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# One-command dev environment setup from a fresh clone.
# Usage: ./scripts/setup.sh
# Requires: conda (miniconda/miniforge), docker, pnpm, git

set -euo pipefail

CYAN='\033[0;36m'; GREEN='\033[0;32m'; RED='\033[0;31m'; NC='\033[0m'
step() { echo -e "${CYAN}▶ $1${NC}"; }
ok()   { echo -e "${GREEN}✓ $1${NC}"; }
die()  { echo -e "${RED}✗ $1${NC}" >&2; exit 1; }

# set_env_kv <file> <key> <value> — set KEY=value, leaving an already-non-blank
# value alone. Substitutes when the key is present (blank or not) and APPENDS when
# it is absent: a plain `sed s|^KEY=.*|` is a silent no-op on a .env that predates
# the key, which would leave the file short of a value compose then refuses to
# start without — telling the user to run this script, which they just did.
set_env_kv() {
  local file="$1" key="$2" value="$3"
  grep -qE "^${key}=..*$" "${file}" && return 0        # already set — keep it
  if grep -qE "^${key}=" "${file}"; then
    sed -i.bak -e "s|^${key}=.*|${key}=${value}|" "${file}" && rm -f "${file}.bak"
  else
    # A hand-edited file may lack a trailing newline; appending blind would splice
    # the key onto the last line and corrupt both.
    [ -s "${file}" ] && [ "$(tail -c1 "${file}" | wc -l)" -eq 0 ] && printf '\n' >> "${file}"
    printf '%s=%s\n' "${key}" "${value}" >> "${file}"
  fi
}

# ── Prerequisites ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Checking prerequisites"
command -v conda  >/dev/null || die "conda not found — install miniconda or miniforge first"
command -v docker >/dev/null || die "docker not found"
command -v pnpm   >/dev/null || die "pnpm not found — run: npm install -g pnpm"
command -v git    >/dev/null || die "git not found"
ok "Prerequisites OK"

# ── Local env files ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Two files (split in #209 so Settings can run extra="forbid"):
#   .env     — infra/compose only (POSTGRES_*, VITE_*); compose substitutes ${...}
#              from it and the postgres service reads it.
#   .env.app — app config (DATABASE_URL, AZURE_*, …); the file Settings reads.
# App code carries no DB credentials (config.py default is credential-less), so
# host-side tooling (alembic, seed, uvicorn) needs DATABASE_URL from .env.app.
# Create both from their templates on first run, then export so child processes
# inherit them regardless of working dir (alembic runs from backend/, so a
# CWD-relative dotenv lookup wouldn't find the root file).
step "Preparing .env / .env.app"
# Local-dev DB credentials are GENERATED here, never shipped in the tracked
# templates (those ship blank — we don't commit credentials, even mock ones).
# The password must match across both files: .env's POSTGRES_PASSWORD (the
# postgres container + the compose-built container DATABASE_URL) and .env.app's
# host-side DATABASE_URL (alembic/seed/uvicorn). user/db are non-secret
# identifiers; only the password is generated.
local_pg_user="dataq"
local_pg_db="dataq"
# Reuse a password already set in .env (so re-runs stay consistent); otherwise
# generate a fresh hex one (URL-safe — no special chars to encode in
# DATABASE_URL). `=..*` matches only a NON-blank value, so a blank line doesn't
# count as "set".
local_pg_password="REDACTED"
if [ -z "${local_pg_password}" ]; then
  local_pg_password="REDACTED"
fi

# Same story for the OpenBao dev-mode root token (ADR 0039), except it must match
# across .env (compose starts the vault with it) AND .env.app (the app authenticates
# with it) — a mismatch 403s every credential read. Reuse whichever file already has
# one so re-runs stay consistent.
local_bao_token="$(sed -n 's/^OPENBAO_TOKEN=\(..*\)$/\1/p' .env 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
if [ -z "${local_bao_token}" ]; then
  local_bao_token="$(sed -n 's/^OPENBAO_TOKEN=\(..*\)$/\1/p' .env.app 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
fi
if [ -z "${local_bao_token}" ]; then
  local_bao_token="$(openssl rand -hex 16 2>/dev/null || date +%s | shasum | cut -c1-32)"
fi

# Create each file from its template if missing, then BACK-FILL the local-dev
# creds whenever the key is still blank — covers a fresh copy AND a pre-existing
# file left blank (e.g. a manual `cp` of the now-blank template). Without the
# back-fill, a blank POSTGRES_PASSWORD trips compose's `${VAR:?}` guard / mismatches
# the host DATABASE_URL.
[ -f .env ] || { cp .env.example .env; ok ".env created from .env.example"; }
if ! grep -qE '^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REDACTED .env; then
  sed -i.bak \
    -e "s|^POSTGRES_USER=.*|POSTGRES_USER=${local_pg_user}|" \
    -e "s|^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REDACTED \
    -e "s|^POSTGRES_DB=.*|POSTGRES_DB=${local_pg_db}|" .env && rm -f .env.bak
  ok ".env local Postgres creds generated"
fi
if ! grep -qE '^OPENBAO_TOKEN=..*$' .env; then
  set_env_kv .env OPENBAO_TOKEN "${local_bao_token}"
  ok ".env OpenBao dev root token generated"
fi

[ -f .env.app ] || { cp .env.app.example .env.app; ok ".env.app created from .env.app.example"; }
if ! grep -qE '^DATABASE_URL=..*$' .env.app; then
  db_url="REDACTED"
  sed -i.bak -e "s|^DATABASE_URL=.*|DATABASE_URL=${db_url}|" .env.app && rm -f .env.app.bak
  ok ".env.app host DATABASE_URL set"
fi
if ! grep -qE '^OPENBAO_TOKEN=..*$' .env.app; then
  set_env_kv .env.app OPENBAO_TOKEN "${local_bao_token}"
  ok ".env.app OpenBao token set (matches .env)"
fi
# Host-side dev (uvicorn/celery on your machine) reads these from .env.app; the
# compose api/worker override the address to the in-network hostname. Appended for
# a .env.app that predates ADR 0039 so a re-run leaves a complete file. SECRET_STORE
# is deliberately NOT rewritten — an existing `redis` value raises at startup with
# the migration path, and silently changing someone's configured mode is worse.
set_env_kv .env.app OPENBAO_ADDR "http://localhost:8200"
set_env_kv .env.app OPENBAO_MOUNT "secret"
set -a
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. ./.env
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. ./.env.app
set +a

# ── Conda environment ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Creating / updating conda environment 'dataq'"
if conda env list | grep -q "^dataq "; then
  conda env update -n dataq -f environment.yml --prune
  ok "Conda env updated"
else
  conda env create -f environment.yml
  ok "Conda env created"
fi

# ── Pre-commit hooks ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# First run compiles the betterleaks secret-scanning hook (language: golang); this
# can take a minute. pre-commit (≥3.0) bootstraps its own Go — no system Go needed.
step "Installing pre-commit hooks"
conda run -n dataq pre-commit install --install-hooks
ok "Pre-commit hooks installed"

# ── Frontend dependencies ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Installing frontend dependencies (pnpm)"
(cd frontend && pnpm install)
ok "Frontend dependencies installed"

# ── Docker services ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Starting Docker services (Postgres, Redis)"
docker compose up -d postgres redis
ok "Docker services started"

# ── Database migrations ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step "Waiting for Postgres to be ready"
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  if docker compose exec -T postgres pg_isready -U dataq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ok "Postgres ready"
    break
  fi
  [ "$i" -eq 30 ] && die "Postgres did not become ready in time"
  sleep 1
done

step "Running Alembic migrations"
conda run -n dataq sh -c "cd backend && alembic upgrade head"
ok "Migrations applied"

# ── Seed data ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Run as a module (-m) so the repo root is on sys.path and `backend.*` imports
# resolve; running the file directly would not put the root on the path.
step "Seeding dev data"
conda run -n dataq python -m backend.scripts.seed_dev
ok "Dev data seeded"

# ── Done ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo ""
echo -e "${GREEN}━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━${NC}"
echo -e "${GREEN}  DataQ dev environment ready!${NC}"
echo -e "${GREEN}━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━${NC}"
echo ""
echo "  Next steps:"
echo "    conda activate dataq"
echo "    docker compose up          # start all services"
echo "    # API: http://localhost:8000/docs"
echo "    # UI:  http://localhost:3000"
echo ""

# Two files (split in #209 so Settings can run extra="forbid"):

#              from it and the postgres service reads it.
#   .env.app — app config (DATABASE_URL, AZURE_*, …); the file Settings reads.
# App code carries no DB credentials (config.py default is credential-less), so
# host-side tooling (alembic, seed, uvicorn) needs DATABASE_URL from .env.app.
# Create both from their templates on first run, then export so child processes
# inherit them regardless of working dir (alembic runs from backend/, so a
# CWD-relative dotenv lookup wouldn't find the root file).
step "Preparing .env / .env.app"
# Local-dev DB credentials are GENERATED here, never shipped in the tracked
# templates (those ship blank — we don't commit credentials, even mock ones).
# The password must match across both files: .env's POSTGRES_PASSWORD (the
# postgres container + the compose-built container DATABASE_URL) and .env.app's
# host-side DATABASE_URL (alembic/seed/uvicorn). user/db are non-secret
# identifiers; only the password is generated.

local_pg_db="dataq"
# Reuse a password already set in .env (so re-runs stay consistent); otherwise

# DATABASE_URL). `=..*` matches only a NON-blank value, so a blank line doesn't
# count as "set".

if [ -z "${local_pg_password}" ]; then

fi

# one so re-runs stay consistent.

if [ -z "${local_bao_token}" ]; then
  local_bao_token="$(sed -n 's/^OPENBAO_TOKEN=\(..*\)$/\1/p' .env.app 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
fi
if [ -z "${local_bao_token}" ]; then
  local_bao_token="$(openssl rand -hex 16 2>/dev/null || date +%s | shasum | cut -c1-32)"
fi

# Create each file from its template if missing, then BACK-FILL the local-dev
# creds whenever the key is still blank — covers a fresh copy AND a pre-existing
# file left blank (e.g. a manual `cp` of the now-blank template). Without the
# back-fill, a blank POSTGRES_PASSWORD trips compose's `${VAR:?}` guard / mismatches
# the host DATABASE_URL.
[ -f .env ] || { cp .env.example .env; ok ".env created from .env.example"; }
if ! grep -qE '^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REDACTED .env; then
  sed -i.bak \
    -e "s|^POSTGRES_USER=.*|POSTGRES_USER=${local_pg_user}|" \
    -e "s|^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REDACTED \
    -e "s|^POSTGRES_DB=.*|POSTGRES_DB=${local_pg_db}|" .env && rm -f .env.bak
  ok ".env local Postgres creds generated"
fi
if ! grep -qE '^OPENBAO_TOKEN=..*$' .env; then
  set_env_kv .env OPENBAO_TOKEN "${local_bao_token}"
  ok ".env OpenBao dev root token generated"
fi

[ -f .env.app ] || { cp .env.app.example .env.app; ok ".env.app created from .env.app.example"; }
if ! grep -qE '^DATABASE_URL=..*$' .env.app; then
  db_url="REDACTED"
  sed -i.bak -e "s|^DATABASE_URL=.*|DATABASE_URL=${db_url}|" .env.app && rm -f .env.app.bak

fi
if ! grep -qE '^OPENBAO_TOKEN=..*$' .env.app; then
  set_env_kv .env.app OPENBAO_TOKEN "${local_bao_token}"
  ok ".env.app OpenBao token set (matches .env)"

# compose api/worker override the address to the in-network hostname. Appended for
# a .env.app that predates ADR 0039 so a re-run leaves a complete file. SECRET_STORE

# the migration path, and silently changing someone's configured mode is worse.
set_env_kv .env.app OPENBAO_ADDR "http://localhost:8200"
set_env_kv .env.app OPENBAO_MOUNT "secret"
set -a

. ./.env
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. ./.env.app
set +a

# First run compiles the betterleaks secret-scanning hook (language: golang); this
